DIRECTION: Classic Circuit Console. Familiar retro desktop puzzle charm remastered with contemporary cinematic 3D quality. A strong left-hand hierarchy holds a crafted silver-and-green block wordmark, an elegant compact microchip-with-keyhole emblem, and a clean vertical menu. The right two-thirds is an inviting three-quarter overhead hero diorama: gray tile corridors, obvious colored keys and locks, a beautifully modeled green explorer with glasses, one red six-legged bug, IC chips and small blue spiral exit. Rich green etched PCB background with restrained branching fine traces and subtle gold-free highlights; satin gray/silver UI frame and one vivid green PLAY button. Strong silvery typographic silhouette readable even at app-icon scale, crisp professional game title design. Beautiful soft studio lighting, realistic material response and ambient occlusion, no excessive bloom. Camera is static, showing the puzzle clearly. Aim for a premium affectionate remake rather than a generic web dashboard.

DIRECTION: Portal and Key. A bold cinematic banner-first main menu, with the upper two-thirds devoted to a beautifully lit panoramic 3D puzzle world and a clean deep-green horizontal brand-and-actions rail across the lower third. This must have a meaningfully different composition from a left-hand vertical menu or a centered tabletop menu. Behind him extend orderly silver-gray square puzzle corridors with red, green and yellow matching keys and locks, tiny black IC chips, one beautifully articulated red bug and a luminous blue concentric-square exit. Emphasize actual craft in materials, subtle cloth seams, hair, glasses, beveled metal, scale and lighting; no excessive glow or epic fantasy fog. The lower rail has a clean ORIGINAL flat graphic emblem: concentric square path integrating a tiny keyhole, with a confident highly legible modern geometric SHADOW CIRCUIT wordmark and small A SHADOW CHAT GAME endorsement at its left; PLAY as the dominant silver/bright green button at the right, LEVELS and SETTINGS quieter beside it. The wordmark is mostly crisp silver-white with a restrained vivid green accent, NOT chunky 3D arcade text.
